generatedProse.concept-context: In the School of Sport, the report follows the familiar introduction, method, results and discussion structure of a journal article. The results section reports what was found, the descriptive and inferential statistics, plainly and without interpretation. The discussion is where you say what the findings mean, how far they can be trusted, and how they sit against existing work. This holds whether the study is a physiology trial, a coaching intervention or a rehabilitation case series. Writing an effect size into the results is right; writing 'this shows the protocol works' into the results is the error this lesson targets.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two sport therapy and rehabilitation students write up the same small return-to-play study and reach the results section.

Tom writes that the treated group returned to training sooner, which shows that the rehab protocol clearly works and that clinics should adopt it. The finding is there, but it is tangled with interpretation and a recommendation. A reader cannot see the plain result on its own, and claims about what it means have arrived before the discussion, where they could be weighed.

Amara writes, in the results, that the treated group returned a stated number of days earlier on average, with the relevant statistic. She saves the reading of that difference for the discussion. There she asks whether the margin is large enough to matter in the clinic, notes that the sample was small and drawn from one sport, and holds back from advising any clinic until the evidence can bear it.

Both found the same result. Only Amara kept the results and the discussion in their proper sections.
generatedProse.summary: In the School of Sport, a report is structured so that each core element does one job: the introduction frames the question, the method makes the study repeatable, the results present the statistics, and the discussion interprets them. You can now use these elements for their proper purpose, tell results apart from discussion, and place a passage in the section where it belongs. With the review, the proposal and the report, you have the three genres that carry research across the School of Sport.

check.body: In the worked example, what did Amara do that Tom did not?

items.text: She reported the finding plainly in the results and saved its interpretation for the discussion.
She found a larger difference between the two groups.
She recommended adopting the rehab protocol more strongly than Tom.
She wrote a longer results section than Tom.

feedback.correct: That's right. Amara kept the plain finding in the results and its interpretation in the discussion.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look at WHERE each student put the finding and its interpretation.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara reported the finding in the results and saved interpretation for the discussion. A bigger difference, a stronger recommendation or more length were not the point.
